3.  26-55328  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on the FY 2026 Continuum of
  Care (CoC) Program Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO).

  A motion was made by Member Scott, seconded by Member Wee, to approve
  recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Wee, Shuford, Scott, Diles III, Brown-Shock, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 6  Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach, McFadzen, Martins, Lock

  • Health Department staff Jospeh Botelho provided an overview presentation
  on the FY2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) that was published on
  June 1, 2026, the funding available is $4,040,000,000. The application due
  date would be August 26, 2026 and award announcements would be
  December 1, 2026.
  • FY 2026 does not include a Permanent Housing cap, but renewal risk
  remains because Tier 1 is.
  • lowered to 60% of ARD, Tier 2 is competitive, and HUD prioritizes $1.3B in
  new TH and SSO projects.
  • HUD is prioritizing measurable reductions in homelessness, particularly
  unsheltered homelessness, and expects CoCs to evaluate renewal projects
  based on their effectiveness in improving housing stability and self-

  Page 2 of 8
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JUNE 9, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  sufficiency.
• The FY 2026 CoC Program increases competition by reducing Tier 1 funding
  to 60% of Annual Renewal Demand (ARD), encouraging CoCs to improve
  project performance, innovation, and accountability.
• HUD aims to restore balance within the CoC system by expanding
  opportunities for Transitional Housing (TH) and Supportive Services Only
  (SSO) projects, including a $1.3 billion set-aside for new projects with priority
  given to these project types.
• HUD is emphasizing treatment, recovery, and supportive services as
  pathways to self-sufficiency, encouraging projects that provide behavioral
  health services, recovery housing, and other wraparound supports.
• CoCs are encouraged to prioritize strategies that promote long-term
  economic independence, including employment, workforce development,
  childcare supports, and transitions to unsubsidized housing.
• Public safety coordination is receiving increased emphasis, with HUD
  encouraging collaboration with law enforcement and local governments to
  reduce encampments and public drug use while connecting individuals to
  housing, treatment, and services.
• HUD emphasizes minimizing trauma associated with homelessness by
  encouraging safety-informed care practices and prioritizing participant safety,
  particularly for youth and survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault,
  dating violence, and stalking.
• CoCs are encouraged to ensure services and housing programs are
  responsive to the needs of vulnerable populations and support safe, trauma-
  informed environments.
• The estimate funding available is:
  o ARD $12,159,623
  o Tier 1 $7,295,774
  o CoC Bonus $1,823,943
  o DV Bonus $1,968,189
  o CoC Planning $607,981
  o UFA Costs $634,789
• These estimates are for planning purposes only and are subject to change
  pending HUD's FY 2026 GIW and Estimated ARD Report.
• FY 2025 Continuum of Care (CoC) awards totaled approximately $3.85
  billion, while FY 2026 NOFO funding availability is approximately $4.04
  billion, representing an increase of about $193 million year-over-year.
• The FY 2026 selection process identifies approximately $1.83 billion in
  priority or floor funding, including $104 million for Domestic Violence Bonus
  projects, $430 million for Permanent Housing projects serving families with
  children, and $1.3 billion for new projects with priority for Transitional
  Housing and Supportive Services Only (SSO).
• After accounting for priority funding, approximately $2.21 billion remains for
  other selections. While FY 2026 does not cap Permanent Housing funding,

  renewal demand may increase due to factors such as first-time renewals of
  YHDP or Special NOFO projects and COLA/FMR adjustments, continuing to

  • Staff discussed the next steps for the FY 2026 CoC competition.
  • A Board member inquired about whether Rapid Rehousing (RRH) is being

4.  26-55329  Recommendation to review and approve the FY 2026 Scoring and Ranking Policy.

  A motion was made by Member Shuford, seconded by Member Brown-Shock,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Wee, Shuford, Scott, Diles III, Brown-Shock, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 6  Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach, McFadzen, Martins, Lock

  • Health Department staff Jospeh Botelho provided an overview presentation
  on the FY 2026 Continuum of Care Scoring and Ranking Policies.
  • HUD requires CoCs to review, assess, and score project applications for
  performance as part of the CoC Program Competition.
  • HUD increases emphasis on objective criteria in project evaluation, including
  cost effectiveness, unit utilization, and spending performance, requiring at
  least 50% of available points (up from 33% in FY 2024).
  • System performance measures, such as returns to homelessness and
  increases in employment income, must account for at least 25% of available
  points (up from at least 20% in FY 2024).
  • Supportive service participation requirements are incorporated into local
  project review and Tier 2 scoring processes to further align project
  performance with service engagement outcomes.
  • Scope and methodology updates added guidance for first-time renewals
  under the Special Unsheltered NOFO, introduced sliding scale scoring, and
  included fiscal performance review adjustments.
  • Metric scoring was revised to a sliding scale and rebalanced to align with FY
  2026 NOFO requirements.
  • New metrics were added for returns to homelessness and supportive service
  participation, while less performance-relevant metrics were removed.
  • HUD requires CoCs to demonstrate a single, coordinated, inclusive, and
  outcome-oriented community process for the solicitation, objective review,
  ranking, and selection of project applications
  • Staff discussed HUD’s process for selecting projects for funding, including
  ranking by project type and threshold criteria. Staff explained how project

  ranking and threshold requirements are used to determine eligibility,
  prioritize funding decisions, and guide the overall selection process, as well
  as why these factors are important in the competitive funding framework.
  • Next steps were discussed.
  • A board member asked whether providers that receive funding are on board
  with the changes. Staff provided a response, city staff have not encountered
  any issues of concerns with providers.

5.  26-55330  Recommendation to review and approve the Long Beach Continuum of Care
  (CoC) Reallocation Policies and Procedures.

  A motion was made by Member Brown-Shock, seconded by Member Amick,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Wee, Shuford, Scott, Diles III, Brown-Shock, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 6  Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach, McFadzen, Martins, Lock

  • Health Department staff Jospeh Botelho provided an overview presentation
  on the Long Beach Continuum of Care Reallocation Policies and
  Procedures.
  • Reallocation allows the CoC to redirect funding from existing renewed
  projects to new projects that better support community priorities and improve
  overall system performance. This may occur voluntarily by the recipient or
  involuntarily when a project does not meet established performance
  standards.
  • HUD requires every CoC to have a documented reallocation process and
  either demonstrate how it is implemented or show that at least 20% of its
  Annual Renewal Demand was reallocated between the FY 2021 and FY
  2026 funding competitions.
  • The revisions strengthen oversight and transparency by clarifying Board
  review, documentation requirements, and subrecipient notification
  procedures for UFA funding shifts and reallocations occurring outside the
  NOFO process.
  • The updated reallocation policies allow funds to support transition or
  replacement projects when permitted by HUD, separate performance
  improvement requirements from reallocation thresholds, and provide clearer
  guidance on when voluntary or involuntary reallocation may occur.
  • Projects are evaluated for renewal eligibility based on performance and
  utilization. High-performing projects (70%+ performance and 90%+
  utilization) remain eligible for full renewal, while lower-performing or
  underutilized projects may face ranking adjustments, partial reallocation, or

  Page 5 of 8
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JUNE 9, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  full reallocation.
  • Projects with chronic underutilization defined as at least 10% underutilization
  for three consecutive years may be subject to partial reallocation, with the
  funding reduction calculated based on the number of underutilized beds or
  service slots.
  • Spend-down performance determines reallocation risk and chronic
  underspending triggers reallocation thresholds.
  • Staff discussed the next steps.
  • A Board member provided feedback for staff regarding meeting packet
  communication. Other members shared concerns for the next two years for
  providers.

6.  26-55331  Recommendation to review and approve the FY 2026 Continuum of Care (CoC)
  Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) Funding Priorities.

  A motion was made by Member Brown-Shock, seconded by Co-Chair Boyce,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Wee, Shuford, Scott, Diles III, Brown-Shock, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 6  Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach, McFadzen, Martins, Lock

  • Health Department staff Jospeh Botelho provided an overview presentation
  on the FY 2026 Continuum of Care Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO)
  Funding Priorities.
  • HUD requires CoCs to have a formal selection process for new/expansion
  funding as part of the CoC Program Competition.
  • The CoC must follow a transparent, objective, and publicly announced
  process to solicit, review, rank, and select project applications, with
  consideration given to how projects improve overall system performance.
  • HUD's annual NOFO determines eligible project types and funding limits for
  new projects, including CoC Bonus and DV Bonus funding opportunities.
  • The FY 2026 NOFO revisions align CoC Bonus and DV Bonus funding with
  HUD eligibility requirements, including limiting DV Bonus solicitations to
  Transitional Housing (TH) projects and prioritizing TH and Supportive
  Services Only (SSO) project types.
  • The updated funding priorities strengthen the competitive review process by
  incorporating HUD eligibility and scoring criteria, preserving Permanent
  Housing (PH) capacity where feasible, and allowing flexibility for PH family
  projects and project transitions to maximize funding competitiveness.
  • For FY 2026, the CoC will prioritize soliciting Transitional Housing (TH) and
  eligible Supportive Services Only (SSO) projects, while limiting DV Bonus

  funding opportunities to TH projects and tracking DV-specific funding
  separately.
  • Although Permanent Housing (PH) for families with children is not a primary
  solicitation focus, HSB may submit or recommend PH family projects when
  necessary to remain competitive for HUD funding or access targeted funding
  opportunities.
  • Staff discussed the next steps.
  • A Board member complimented staff member Joseph Botelho on the quality
  and execution of his presentation.

7.  26-55332  Recommendation to review and discuss proposed updates to the Long Beach
  Continuum of Care (CoC) Governance Charter and Bylaws.

  A motion was made by Member Brown-Shock, seconded by Member Shuford,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Wee, Shuford, Scott, Diles III, Brown-Shock, Boyce, Amick
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 6  Topolewski, Tan, Rockenbach, McFadzen, Martins, Lock

  • This item was carried over from last month's agenda and is scheduled to
  return for approval at the July meeting.
  • City staff provided an update regarding the Charter in relation to the Notice
  of Funding Opportunity (NOFO). Staff reported that HUD indicated last year
  that Continuums of Care (CoCs) would receive scoring consideration based
  on board composition. Specifically, HUD identified the inclusion of
  representatives from the following sectors: elected officials, the business
  community (such as a Business Improvement District representative), law
  enforcement, recovery housing or sober living providers, behavioral health or
  primary healthcare providers, workforce development organizations, and
  local court systems that manage assisted outpatient treatment or other civil
  commitment programs. Additional points may be awarded for including
  representatives from these sectors.
  • Staff noted that they are not recommending changes to the current board
  structure at this time and do not believe the potential scoring benefit would
  justify a significant restructuring of the board. However, staff felt the matter
  warranted discussion by the Board. Potential concerns associated with
  expanding board membership include challenges related to maintaining a
  quorum.
  • Board members provided feedback on the item and requested that it be
  brought back as a separate agenda item for discussion by the full Board at
  next month's meeting.
